guides.title: Servant Leadership Bible Study
guides.subtitle: The Basin and the Towel
guides.audience: Elder teams, leadership cohorts, and church staff
guides.intro: Six weeks in the Scriptures that define greatness as the willingness to be last. Each session names the real question, slows down one passage, and ends with a practice and a verse to carry. For leaders who want to be formed, not only informed.

sessions.title: What Is Servant Leadership?
sessions.headline: The Word We Domesticated
sessions.bigIdea: Jesus does not correct the desire for greatness. He redefines it as the willingness to be last.
discussion: Where have I used 'servant leadership' for authority that costs me nothing?
What does James and John's request reveal about how I picture greatness?
Read v.45. What does it cost to lead the way the Son of Man led?
sessions.practice: Name one task you delegated because it was beneath you. Take it back this week.
sessions.prayer: Lord, expose where I have dressed ambition in the language of service.

memoryVerse.text: Whoever would be great among you must be your servant

sessions.title: Worldly vs. Biblical Leadership
sessions.headline: Constantine in the Conference Room
sessions.bigIdea: Israel wanted a king 'like the other nations.' The church keeps wanting a leadership model like the other organizations.
discussion: Where has our leadership culture borrowed from the corporation rather than the kingdom?
What does God grant Israel — and what does He warn it will cost?
Which 'like the other nations' assumption is most embedded in how we lead?
sessions.practice: Audit your last three leadership decisions: kingdom-shaped or empire-shaped?
sessions.prayer: Father, unteach us the instincts we learned from the empire.

memoryVerse.text: They have rejected me from being king

sessions.title: Jesus Washes the Disciples' Feet
sessions.headline: What Jesus Did With a Basin
sessions.bigIdea: The foot-washing happens at the moment of maximum authority. The basin is the exercise of power, not its surrender.
discussion: Why does John tell us Jesus knew 'all things' had been given Him before He knelt?
What is your basin — the lowly thing your position let you stop doing?
Peter resists being served. What does that reveal about receiving, not just giving?
sessions.practice: Do one literal basin task no one expects of someone in your role.
sessions.prayer: Jesus, let me lead from the floor where You knelt.

memoryVerse.text: I have given you an example

sessions.title: Humility in Leadership
sessions.headline: Authority That Runs Downward
sessions.bigIdea: The mind of Christ moves down — emptying, humbling, obeying — before it is exalted.
discussion: Trace the downward steps in vv.6–8. Where am I unwilling to descend?
How does v.9 reframe ambition?
What would 'this mind' change about how I run a meeting?
sessions.practice: Identify one place you hold power for security's sake. Distribute it.
sessions.prayer: Form in me the mind that moves down before it moves up.

memoryVerse.text: He humbled himself

sessions.title: Leading Through Weakness
sessions.headline: The Wound as Credential
sessions.bigIdea: Treasure in jars of clay. The leader's weakness is the container for power, not the obstacle to it.
discussion: What failure have I hidden that, named, could pastor someone through theirs?
Why does Paul boast in weakness rather than competence?
Where does my jar of clay need to crack so the treasure shows?
sessions.practice: Tell one leader you are forming about a real failure and what it taught you.
sessions.prayer: Make my weakness the place Your power is seen.

memoryVerse.text: My power is made perfect in weakness

sessions.title: Building Servant Leadership Habits
sessions.headline: Rebuilding the Towel Habit
sessions.bigIdea: Servant leadership is not a conviction. It is a calendar. It survives only as built structure.
discussion: What one structure would make servant leadership unavoidable for me?
Who have I made unnecessary this season — and is that a win or a threat?
What is the next basin I am avoiding?
sessions.practice: Write your own 'towel habit' — one recurring practice that keeps you on the floor. Schedule it.
sessions.prayer: Keep me on the floor, Lord, long after the feeling fades.

memoryVerse.text: Blessed are you if you do them

guides.title: Elder Training Manual
guides.subtitle: Shepherds, Not a Board
guides.audience: Pastors raising elders, and the men being raised
guides.intro: How to Develop Church Elders. God screens for the man, not the resume — of roughly twenty qualifications, only one is a skill. Eight sessions through the biblical qualifications, plus a four-stage process to identify, examine, and ordain men who will last.
process: OBSERVE (0–6 months): he watches elders shepherd hard cases and debriefs each one.
EXAMINE (6–12 months): character, household, and doctrine tested openly — his wife and grown children testify.
SHEPHERD (12–24 months): he carries real souls under a seasoned elder's cover.
ORDAIN & REPRODUCE (24+ months): set apart with the charge to raise his own replacement.

sessions.title: Biblical Qualifications of an Elder
sessions.headline: We Recruited the Wrong Men
sessions.bigIdea: God screens for the man, not the resume. Of roughly twenty qualifications, only one is a skill.
discussion: What accusation could be credibly made about me right now?
Where is my public life diverging from my private one?
Which single qualification exposes me most?
sessions.practice: Ask your spouse: 'Where am I not the man people think I am?'
sessions.prayer: Search me and know my heart.

memoryVerse.text: Above reproach

sessions.title: The Elder and His Family
sessions.headline: The Household First
sessions.bigIdea: The home is the proving ground. A man who cannot shepherd his house cannot shepherd God's.
discussion: What does my home reveal about my fitness to lead?
Where do I lead the church better than my family?
Who in my house would vouch for me — and who wouldn't?
sessions.practice: Have the conversation with your children you have been avoiding.
sessions.prayer: Make me faithful in the small kingdom first.

memoryVerse.text: He must manage his own household well

sessions.title: An Elder's Character and Appetites
sessions.headline: Where Elders Fall First
sessions.bigIdea: Money, temper, and substance are where elders fall before anyone sees it.
discussion: Which appetite do I manage rather than master?
Who can ask me about my money and my temper?
What private drift would disqualify me if it surfaced?
sessions.practice: Give one person full permission to ask about your finances.
sessions.prayer: Master in me what I have only managed.

memoryVerse.text: Not greedy for gain

sessions.title: Able to Teach
sessions.headline: Truth With a Gentle Spirit
sessions.bigIdea: The one required competence is holding truth and correcting error with gentleness.
discussion: Can I hold sound doctrine and a gentle spirit at once?
Do I correct to win or to restore?
Where does my teaching wound rather than heal?
sessions.practice: Teach one truth to one person, gently, in their hardness.
sessions.prayer: Give me truth in a spirit that heals.

memoryVerse.text: Hold firm to the trustworthy word

sessions.title: Tested by Time, Not Talent
sessions.headline: Not a Recent Convert
sessions.bigIdea: Time is a qualification. Conceit is the trap laid for the man elevated too soon.
discussion: Have I been tested by time and trouble, or only by talent?
Where is conceit already at work in me?
What season most proved or exposed me?
sessions.practice: Name the season that most tested you. What did it form?
sessions.prayer: Guard me from the conceit of the quickly elevated.

memoryVerse.text: Lest he become puffed up

sessions.title: Reputation Outside the Church
sessions.headline: The Watching World
sessions.bigIdea: Reputation outside the church is part of the qualification. The world is a witness.
discussion: What do people unimpressed by me say about me?
Where does my outside reputation contradict my inside one?
Who outside the church would I least want interviewed about me?
sessions.practice: Ask a non-Christian who knows you for one honest critique.
sessions.prayer: Let my life ring true where no one expects it.

memoryVerse.text: Well thought of by outsiders

sessions.title: Shepherd the Flock Among You
sessions.headline: Among You, Not Over You
sessions.bigIdea: Elders lead by example among the flock, not by domineering over it.
discussion: Do I lead among the people or over them?
Whose soul am I actually carrying this month?
Where am I domineering and calling it leading?
sessions.practice: Spend one hour this week with the hardest sheep to love.
sessions.prayer: Give me a shepherd's heart for the ones who cost me most.

memoryVerse.text: Being examples to the flock

sessions.title: Raising the Next Elder
sessions.headline: Ordain to Reproduce
sessions.bigIdea: Ordination is a starting line. Every elder is charged from day one to raise his replacement.
discussion: Who am I currently forming to take my place?
If I were gone, who would carry this flock?
What am I doing that only I can do — and why?
sessions.practice: Choose one man to begin walking through this manual.
sessions.prayer: Let me raise the elder who outlasts me.

memoryVerse.text: Entrust to faithful men

guides.title: Deacon Training Manual
guides.subtitle: Born From a Complaint About Widows
guides.audience: Deacons, deacon candidates, and the pastors training them
guides.intro: The biblical role of a deacon, the qualifications of 1 Timothy 3, and the Acts 6 origin of servant ministry. The diaconate was born when widows were overlooked — so that no one falls through the cracks of a growing church, and the word and prayer are protected.

sessions.title: The Origin of the Deacon (Acts 6)
sessions.headline: Service Is the DNA
sessions.bigIdea: The diaconate was born when widows were overlooked. The office exists so that no one falls through the cracks of a growing church — and so the word and prayer are protected.
discussion: What 'overlooked widow' exists in our church right now?
How does serving tables protect the ministry of the word?
Why does the text say the number of disciples multiplied right after this?
sessions.practice: Find one person currently overlooked by the church's systems. Serve them this week.
sessions.prayer: Lord, give me eyes for the ones who are being missed.

memoryVerse.text: It is not right that we should neglect the word

sessions.title: Qualifications of a Deacon
sessions.headline: Tested First, Then Trusted
sessions.bigIdea: Deacons are dignified, honest, not greedy, tested, and faithful at home. The same character bar as elders — different function, not lower standard.
discussion: Which qualification do I most need to grow in?
Where is my speech double-tongued — one thing here, another there?
Am I tested, or just available?
sessions.practice: Let yourself be tested in one concrete responsibility before seeking the office.
sessions.prayer: Make me trustworthy in small things first.

memoryVerse.text: Let them also be tested first

sessions.title: What a Deacon Actually Does
sessions.headline: The Ministry of the Practical
sessions.bigIdea: Deacons handle the practical care of the body — benevolence, logistics, mercy — so the church's life holds together and the word goes unhindered.
discussion: What practical needs in our church are currently unmet?
How is 'serving tables' actually spiritual work?
Where do I think a task is beneath me?
sessions.practice: Take ownership of one unglamorous, unseen need this week.
sessions.prayer: Teach me to find dignity in the hidden work.

memoryVerse.text: Phoebe, a servant of the church

sessions.title: Deacons and Unity
sessions.headline: Guardians of the Body's Peace
sessions.bigIdea: The first deacons were appointed to resolve a dispute that threatened unity. Deacons are peacemakers who keep grumbling from becoming division.
discussion: Where is grumbling growing in our church that I could help heal?
Am I a source of unity or friction?
How do I handle a complaint brought to me?
sessions.practice: Address one quiet conflict before it spreads.
sessions.prayer: Make me an agent of peace, not a carrier of complaint.

memoryVerse.text: Eager to maintain the unity of the Spirit

sessions.title: The Deacon's Reward and the Long View
sessions.headline: A Good Standing for Those Who Serve
sessions.bigIdea: Those who serve well gain a good standing and great boldness in the faith. Hidden service is seen by God and forms the servant into Christ's likeness.
discussion: Am I serving for the standing of God or the notice of people?
What boldness has faithful service grown in me?
Could I serve for a decade unseen?
sessions.practice: Do one act of service this week that no one will ever know about.
sessions.prayer: Let me be content to be seen by You alone.

memoryVerse.text: They gain a good standing for themselves

guides.title: How to Develop Leaders in the Church
guides.subtitle: Reproduce, Do Not Retain
guides.audience: Anyone responsible for raising other leaders
guides.intro: How to spot, train, delegate to, and release new leaders so your ministry reproduces. The leader who cannot be replaced has failed at the one thing leaders are for.

sessions.title: How to Spot Potential Leaders
sessions.headline: Adopt a Posture of Looking
sessions.bigIdea: Jesus prayed all night, then named twelve ordinary men. Leaders are spotted on your knees, not in your org chart.
discussion: Who am I overlooking because they don't look like a leader?
Am I praying for laborers or just recruiting volunteers?
What gift have I failed to call out in someone?
sessions.practice: Write five names of people with unproven gifting. Pray over them this week.
sessions.prayer: Lord of the harvest, show me whom You are raising up.

memoryVerse.text: He chose twelve

sessions.title: Why Delegation Is Discipleship
sessions.headline: Delegation Is Discipleship
sessions.bigIdea: Jethro's rebuke still lands: the leader who keeps everything destroys himself and the people. Hand away what forms people.
discussion: What am I holding that someone else should carry?
Do I delegate to get free or to set someone free?
What am I afraid will happen if I let go?
sessions.practice: Hand off one meaningful responsibility — and stay close enough to disciple them through it.
sessions.prayer: Teach me to give away the work that makes leaders.

memoryVerse.text: You will surely wear yourself out
